name: Berry and Mint
uses: specialty beverages, contemporary skincare, creative retail
rationale: A cool sage carries the interface while a ripe cranberry marks what matters. The two sit nearly opposite on the colour wheel, so the accent reads instantly without fighting the calm primary; lemon gives the mark a soft lift on dark grounds.

name: Oxblood and Fern
uses: wine merchants, apothecaries, heritage hotels, members' clubs
rationale: The darker half of Berry and Mint: deep oxblood leads, and sage softens it as the single secondary hue. Warm jasmine keeps the logo glowing on the red-black ink.

name: Citrus Market
uses: fresh food, local markets, community initiatives
rationale: Leafy green is dependable enough for every button, and the orange accent is loud enough to sell. Lime-yellow tansy finishes the citrus set in the mark.

name: Clear Horizon
uses: consulting, education, B2B services
rationale: Steel blue keeps the original calm. The v1 palette had no second hue, so a warm nutmeg from the library adds a quiet complementary accent for focus and highlights. Gold is reserved for the mark.

name: Eclipse Rose
uses: law firms, private clinics, boutique consultancies, wedding services
rationale: Clear Horizon's deep navy becomes the lead, warmed by a dusty rose accent. A pale sky-blue spark gives the mark a crisp highlight on ink without adding another warm tone.

name: Coastal Herbarium
uses: botanical skincare, garden studios, wellness retreats
rationale: Pine teal stays the anchor. Seagrass sat too close in hue to act as an accent, so a heather-purple orchid from the library plays that role, like pressed flowers on a green page. Cane sugar keeps the sandy warmth in the mark.

name: Seagrass and Clay
uses: wellness apps, outdoor retreats, surf and swim schools, plant-based food
rationale: The brighter green-teal from Coastal Herbarium leads, balanced by a sunbaked clay accent. Cane sugar ties both to the shoreline.

name: Desert Sky
uses: travel, interiors, lifestyle brands
rationale: Dusty sky blue and sun-warmed copper are complementary, so the accent is unmistakable while both stay soft. Sunlit clay gives the mark a desert-light highlight.

name: Brown Study
uses: independent bookshops, coffee roasters, leather goods, editorial publishing
rationale: Desert Sky's deep brown leads and its blue becomes the cool accent, giving a library-and-leather feel. Bright gold is the signal light in the mark.

name: Electric Current
uses: digital products, creative technology, music events
rationale: Saturated cobalt drives the interface and a voltage-yellow accent marks what matters; in light mode the yellow deepens to gold so it stays readable. Greek Blue becomes the cyan spark in the mark, like an arc of current.

name: Aegean Pop
uses: travel apps, beach clubs, creator tools, summer events
rationale: Electric Current's cyan becomes the lead, paired with a raspberry pink accent from the library for holiday energy. Gold remains the logo highlight.

name: Forest Ledger
uses: sustainable finance, conservation, outdoor services
rationale: A muted forest green keeps the interface restrained. Royal Oakleaf was too close in hue and too soft to act as an accent, so a sienna from the library takes that role, like copper fittings on a ledger. Cane sugar is the warm mark highlight.

name: Indigo Linen
uses: textiles, artisan homewares, boutique stationery
rationale: Deep indigo leads and a soft clay-linen accent tempers it. The accent is deliberately quiet, so the indigo stays the hero; gold thread lights up the mark.

name: Ink and Poppy
uses: editorial identities, galleries, event posters
rationale: Poppy red on ink stays the signature. The v1 palette had no second hue, so a lapis blue from the library becomes the accent and focus colour, keeping focus rings from reading as errors. Bright gold completes a poster-like primary set in the mark.

name: Lavender Atelier
uses: beauty studios, independent publishing, creative services
rationale: Sumptuous purple keeps the atelier mood. The v1 sage was too grey to work as an accent and berry tones blurred into the purple, so a soft apricot from the library becomes the accent; in light mode it deepens to a burnt clay. Jasmine lifts the mark.

name: Midnight Brass
uses: boutique finance, watches, architectural practices
rationale: Midnight navy with a brass accent is the identity, so brass stays in the UI even though it sits near the warning amber; warnings are moved further toward orange. A cool sky spark keeps the mark crisp on ink.

name: Midnight Lime
uses: developer tools, experimental music, digital exhibitions
rationale: Near-black navy and acid lime are built for dark mode, where the lime accent glows. In light mode the lime deepens to olive to stay readable. Tangerine gives the mark a second signal.

name: Monochrome Foundry
uses: architecture portfolios, industrial services, photography
rationale: Graphite is the primary, so buttons and active marks are near-black in light mode and pale grey in dark mode. A single clear blue from the library is the only hue, for links in charts, focus and highlights. Gold is the mark's spark.

name: Moss and Lemon
uses: plant shops, natural home goods, creative workshops
rationale: The v1 greens were too grey to carry buttons, so a livelier library moss leads, with a dusty rose accent like a flowering plant. Lemon meringue stays as the logo highlight.

name: Nordic Workshop
uses: industrial design, software tools, professional portfolios
rationale: A barely-blue grey primary keeps the interface almost monochrome, so the burnt-orange accent does all the signalling, like a safety mark on a workbench. Pale lemon lights the mark.

name: Orchard Harvest
uses: farm shops, cider packaging, rural hospitality
rationale: Orchard green leads. The v1 browns and golds would muddy into the warning amber as accents, so a plum from the library ripens the palette instead. Kikuchiba gold stays as the harvest-light spark.

name: Plum After Dark
uses: evening venues, fashion campaigns, premium cosmetics
rationale: Amethyst leads and a neon cyan accent cuts through the dark like stage light. Magenta sat too close to amethyst to work in the interface, so it moves to the mark, where it still reads on ink and amethyst.

name: Rosewood Archive
uses: bookshops, heritage hospitality, editorial brands
rationale: Wine red stays the anchor. A deep library teal is the accent, the classic bookbinding pairing, and golden beige gilds the mark.

name: Saffron Press
uses: independent publishing, cultural events, food journals
rationale: Goldenrod leads; in light mode it deepens to an ochre that can carry white labels. A Baltic blue from the library is the cool counterweight for focus and highlights. Tangerine warms the mark.

name: Strawberry Studio
uses: friendly consumer brands, stationery, family services
rationale: Royal plum gives the playful palette a steady base for buttons and a leafy seagrass green is the accent. Strawberry pink blurred into the plum as an accent, so it becomes the fruit in the mark.

name: Sunwashed Stone
uses: interiors, handmade goods, slow-living brands
rationale: Weathered terracotta leads on plain stone-grey surfaces. A deep library teal is the complementary accent, and sunlit clay warms the mark.

name: Terracotta Table
uses: restaurants, ceramics, specialty food packaging
rationale: Brick terracotta and dark olive set the table; the olive accent is deliberately deep, like oil and herbs against clay. Sunlit clay gives the mark its glow.

name: Tidal Signal
uses: coastal tourism, watersports, transport brands
rationale: Sea teal and signal-flag coral are complementary, so the accent never blends into teal controls. Bright gold is the buoy light in the mark.

name: Tomato and Basil
uses: restaurants, food delivery, recipe apps, delis
rationale: A ripe tomato red drives calls to action and a basil green accent keeps it fresh. Because the primary is red, danger moves toward crimson and always carries an icon and a word.

name: Emerald Exchange
uses: fintech, banking apps, investment platforms, sustainability reporting
rationale: Emerald signals growth and stability; a deep violet accent keeps highlights and focus apart from the green. Success shifts toward teal so it never reads as a brand button.

name: Velvet Bloom
uses: beauty brands, florists, fragrance, wedding stationery
rationale: Velvet rose leads and an iridescent violet accent adds a cool shimmer. Jasmine gives the mark a warm petal highlight.

name: Ultraviolet Fern
uses: gaming, esports, kids' learning apps, creative communities
rationale: Ultraviolet and fern green sit far apart on the wheel, so the accent pops against violet controls. Bright gold adds a third signal in the mark.
